title: 👁️ Pixtral Large 2502 arrives on OpenRouter — a model that sees images and documents!
body: 👁️ Pixtral Large 2502 arrives on OpenRouter — a model that sees images and documents!

Mistral's large vision model, Pixtral Large 2502, arrived on the OpenRouter platform on November 20, becoming available to developers through a single interface at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens.

The model itself is not entirely new: it is the February 2025 version of Mistral's large multimodal model, successor to the November 2024 version, and what is new is its availability now via OpenRouter through a single provider, Amazon Bedrock.

The model accepts text and images together as inputs, reading documents, charts and natural images, then replying in written text, and its context window is 128,000 tokens — enough to read long documents in one go.

But it has clear limits: it does not support tool or function calling, and does not enforce JSON formatting on its outputs — it is a powerful visual reader, not an agent that carries out multi-step tasks.
Its speed via the current provider reaches about 69 tokens per second, with a response time of about one second, and its uptime over the past three days was 99.99%, according to the platform's data.
Simply put: a large French model that sees images and documents and explains them to you is now closer to the developer's hand — just change the model name in your request and it works.
Is a model that reads images and documents enough for you, or do you need one that carries out tasks too?
